text:
Connor McDavid has a point in all 17 of Edmonton's games: 10 goals and 34 assists. We have him at 95% to make it 18 tonight, which is about as close to certain as a hockey number gets. The Canucks, meanwhile, have seven points all season and arrive winless in four, outscored 18-10, after a 6-2 loss in Winnipeg. Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis wrote that Manny Malhotra called out the team's "lack of effort" after that one. Our playoff simulations give Vancouver about 0.1%.

The matchup that worries us most for Vancouver is in its own crease. Leevi Meriläinen has stopped .847 over his last five starts, 4.1 goals worse than expected, after finishing 17.9 below expected last season. He faces an Oilers power play creating 0.88 expected goals a game, against a Canucks penalty kill allowing 0.91. Evan Bouchard has 13 points in six games against Vancouver and goals in three straight.

There's a caveat on the Edmonton side. The Oilers are +19 in goal difference on chances worth +4.4, with 18.5 more goals than their shots usually produce, and they've dropped their last two, including a 5-4 home loss to Anaheim on Thursday. With Zach Hyman out (neck), Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Kapanen and Nugent-Hopkins, and Kasperi Kapanen has moved onto the top power play. Kapanen is our sleeper, 50% for a point against a pace that says 39%.

For Vancouver, Filip Hronek is one point from 300 and one goal from 50, and Brock Boeser has seven points in six games against Edmonton. The two met twice in late September, a 6-5 Vancouver overtime win and a 9-7 Edmonton win. Our numbers have it 3.59 to 2.55 Oilers.
headline: McDavid has a point in every game. Vancouver has seven.

hunch.text: Vancouver probably loses, but Hronek gets his 300th point on a night when the Oilers' goalies give up a few too.
